input: Write a due diligence memo on Canva

business.claim: Canva describes itself as a free online visual communications and collaboration platform with drag-and-drop design tools, templates, stock media and formats spanning presentations, social graphics, posters, apparel and video; it is available on desktop, web, iOS and Android.
The business uses a freemium subscription model: Canva's US pricing page lists a free plan at US$0, Pro at US$144/year per person, and Business at US$250/year per person; Enterprise is sales-led.
Canva targets individuals, small businesses, schools, nonprofits and global enterprises; the company says its Enterprise product is used by 95% of the Fortune 500.
Canva says it operates in more than 190 countries and over 100 languages, with localised content, payment methods, templates and campaigns for regional markets.
Canva expanded beyond its original visual-design suite in 2025 through a connected AI-powered Creative Operating System and the relaunch of professional-creative application Affinity.

traction.claim: Company claim: Canva reported 260 million people using Canva every month in 2025 and $3.5 billion in revenue.

Company claim: In June 2025 Canva reported more than 230 million users in 190 countries, more than 24 million subscribers, annual recurring revenue above $3 billion, and teams at Atlassian, NYSE and HP using Canva.
Company claim: Canva said 100 million teachers, students and education leaders used Canva each month in 2025, across a community in more than 190 countries.

Company claim: Canva reported that more than 25 billion designs had been created and named Skyscanner, Warner Music, American Airlines, Ingram Micro and Eaton among organizational users or customers in its expansion materials.

Company claim: Canva said its team-adoption rate quadrupled in the twelve months to September 2021 and that Zoom, Salesforce, Marriott, PayPal and American Airlines were using Canva as Enterprise customers.
Company claim: More than one million people signed up for Affinity in its first four days after Canva made the application free.

team.claim: Melanie Perkins is Canva co-founder and CEO; Cliff Obrecht is a co-founder and COO; Cameron Adams is co-founder and Chief Product Officer.

Prior-company context: Perkins and Obrecht were running school-yearbook business Fusion Books when they met Cameron Adams; Adams had previously worked with Lars Rasmussen, one of the creators of Google Maps.
Duncan Clark is Canva's Head of Europe and co-founder of data-visualisation platform Flourish, which became part of Canva in 2021.
Company claim: Canva said it expanded its global team by nearly 40% by June 2025 and operated campuses in Melbourne, London, Austin and San Francisco.
Canva's November 2026 team announcement was issued by co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins and describes a reorganisation of Product, Growth and Platform into one Product organisation.

funding.claim: Canva announced a US$200 million funding round led by T. Rowe Price, with strategic and existing investors including Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree; the round implied a US$40 billion valuation.

Canva announced a US$60 million round and a new US$6 billion valuation, up from US$3.2 billion; the company identified Blackbird and Sequoia Capital China as lead investors and listed Felicis, Bond Capital and General Catalyst among participants.
Canva announced a US$40 million round valuing the company at US$1 billion; the announcement named Sequoia China, Blackbird Ventures and Felicis Ventures as investors.

Last publicly reported valuation located: Forbes said an August 2025 employee stock sale valued Canva at US$42 billion, above its US$40 billion September 2021 peak; Inc. separately reported the August 2025 employee stock sale at US$42 billion.

Aggregator data: Fireround records 10 announced Canva rounds totaling approximately US$553.6 million and lists the September 2021 US$200 million round as the latest announced financing round in its profile.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim: Canva reported annualised revenue of US$2.5 billion and its seventh year of profitability in December 2024.
Company claim: Canva reported US$3.5 billion of 2025 revenue.
Canva's CEO said growth had slowed for the first time in a decade; TechCrunch reported that Canva cut its revenue-growth forecast from 30% to 20% amid ballooning AI costs.

Canva announced that 1,271 people, or 22% of the company, would be impacted by restructuring; affected staff were offered at least six months' salary, twelve months of healthcare where available, and career support.
Canva's 2026 restructuring announcement says the company had teams across 37 countries and would reduce subspecialisation, consolidate layers and increase in-person collaboration.

Inc. reported that Canva's internal valuation was revised down approximately 17% to US$35 billion in 2026 and that the company was managing higher AI compute costs by redesigning its architecture and building its own models for specific workflows.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Regulatory action: ASIC issued A$792,000 of infringement notices to four Canva Group entities—Canva Pty, Canva Operations Pty, Canva Trading Pty and Fusion Books Pty—for allegedly failing to lodge FY2024 financial reports by the April 30, 2025 deadline; each entity paid A$198,000. Canva said the consolidated report was lodged March 27, 2026 and that it was now up to date.

reputation.claim: Customer-review aggregator Trustpilot showed Canva at 4.0/5 from about 8,300 reviews, with 5,416 reviews in the prior 12 months; its platform summary praised usability and design tools but cited slow or difficult customer support and frustration that many assets require paid plans.
Customer-review aggregator G2 showed Canva at 4.7/5 from 8,377 reviews, with 84% five-star and 13% four-star ratings.

Employee-review aggregator Blind showed Canva at 3.8/5 from 485 reviews; management was its lowest category at 3.2/5, while work-life balance was highest at 4.0/5. Recent reviews were mixed, citing strong colleagues and benefits alongside concerns about AI direction, management and the effect of layoffs.

Employee-review aggregator Glassdoor displayed 61% positive business outlook, 3.1/5 for senior management and a recent six-month ratings trend of roughly 3.7 to 4.1 across 10 reviews; its AI summary cited praise for collaboration but concerns about politics, shifting priorities and burnout.

red_flags.claim: Growth and execution risk: Canva said growth slowed for the first time in a decade, while TechCrunch reported a revenue-growth forecast reduction from 30% to 20% amid higher AI costs.
Workforce risk: the company announced restructuring affecting 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, only months after reporting strong user and revenue growth.
Valuation risk: Inc. reported an internal valuation reduction of about 17% to US$35 billion in 2026, from the US$42 billion employee-sale valuation reported for August 2025.
Compliance risk: ASIC infringement notices totaling A$792,000 were paid by four Canva Group entities for late FY2024 financial-report lodgements.

Reputation risk: Trustpilot's review summary identified recurring customer-service and paid-feature complaints, while Blind and Glassdoor data showed weaker employee sentiment around management and direction than around product, colleagues or work-life balance.

output.verdict: Canva shows unusually strong product scale and distribution: a global freemium platform with company-reported 260 million monthly users, US$3.5 billion of 2025 revenue, broad enterprise penetration and a long-tenured founding team. The investment case needs a closer look at the 2026 growth slowdown, AI cost structure, internal valuation reset, 22% restructuring, late-reporting penalties and mixed management/customer-support sentiment before relying on the historical growth and US$42 billion private valuation.
